subject: Urban Planning
title: Robert Moses and the Destruction of the Bronx
description: A fast breakdown of Robert Moses and the Destruction of the Bronx for builders.

hook.text: Robert Moses built 13 expressways through New York City. He demolished 250,000 homes to do it.

buildup.text: The Cross Bronx Expressway alone displaced 60,000 residents, cutting neighborhoods in half with a six-lane trench.

discovery.text: Moses chose routes through minority neighborhoods deliberately. He called it 'slum clearance.'

twist.text: He never held elected office. He controlled 12 public authorities and spent $27 billion without voter approval.

climax.text: Jane Jacobs stopped him from building a highway through Greenwich Village. It was his first public defeat.

punchline.text: One man destroyed more neighborhoods than any war. No one voted for him.

quiz.question: How many homes did Robert Moses demolish for his highway projects?
